a1_dyke: The Lamp Road proper is nine feet of dwarf paving under a barrel roof, with a lamp station cut into the wall every mile. Every station you pass has been lit two hours before the charts allow, and the brackets have been wiped down. Ossa checks the third one against her father's timings and then stops checking them aloud.
a1_dyke_top: The crown of the road runs dead straight for four miles, which means that it can be seen along its entire length by anything at all standing at either end of it. Dellach mentions this once, quietly, and then walks the remainder with his shield off his back and his eyes forward. Nothing appears at either end, which is not the same thing as nothing being there.
a1_dyke_low: The drainage gallery runs alongside the paving at four feet high and full of spring water, which hides the company completely and costs it every yard. Halt and Weem take the barrow through on their knees in relay. By the far end everybody is wet to the waist and moving considerably worse than they were.
a1_gibbet: The fourth station has a courier's barrow parked neatly against the wall with its load still roped. On the lamp bracket somebody has hung a Warden's shield with the paint scraped off it. Cut into the post below the bracket is a tally of nine strokes with the ninth struck through, and the dust is still sitting in the grooves.
a1_gibbet_mark: The tally comes out of the post in a single wedge of stone, and Ilsabet lays it down beside the mark she carried out of the Barrow Moor last autumn for comparison. The two match stroke for stroke, including a flaw in the third stroke where the chisel skipped and was not corrected. Whoever keeps this count keeps both of them, and has kept them for a long time.
a1_sluice: At the cistern dip a spring has come through the roof and filled forty feet of road to chest height, which the charts do not mention. The lamps on both sides of the flood are still burning, two of them below the water line, which should not be possible and evidently is. The water is not cold enough to be honest about its depth.
a1_sluice_wade: Chest-deep in spring water at a temperature that ends all argument, with the rope line taut between two brackets and Ossa holding her lamp-pole overhead with both arms the entire way. Kettle counts everybody through twice. The second count is the one that matters to her, and nobody comments on it.
a1_sluice_round: An hour is lost in the maintenance crawl and everybody comes out dry to the knee, which on this road is a bargain. At the crawl's far grating you get the first clear sight of the Marchgate two miles on, and all nine of its lamps are lit, and it is three hours before they should be.
a1_sluice_ward: Salt and glass and Ilsabet's flat working voice, and forty feet of cistern crusting over hard enough to bear a man's weight for slightly under two minutes. The company crosses without stopping, because stopping is specifically what the working cannot survive. On the far side she sits down on the paving and will not be helped up.
a1_moor: The surface stair goes up over the mountain's shoulder in a whiteout, cut for dwarves who did not mind exposure and drifted over since. There are cornices on the left hand and nothing whatsoever on the right, and the wind arrives in shoves rather than gusts. Ossa has been over it twice and does not pretend to like it.
a1_moor_slow: The slow way is roped in line, with Vurma reading the snow ahead and Ossa's pole probing every step of the drift. Six hours buys two miles and nobody is lost, which Vurma considers an entirely reasonable exchange rate. The company arrives at the old workings with the light going and its legs gone.
a1_moor_fast: The fast way works admirably until Weem puts a leg through a snow bridge over a drainage shaft and hangs in his own harness for eleven minutes while three people work out how to lift him. The saved hour is spent entirely on the lifting. Afterwards nobody suggests that the hour was ever real.
a1_moor_path: Something has beaten a sledge trail flat through the drift, days old and as wide as a door, running down the shoulder toward the road. There are small hard bootprints on both flanks of it. The snow in the trail smells of lamp oil, which at this altitude and this temperature is a considerable amount of lamp oil.
a1_drag: The sledge cache at the trail's end has been organised by somebody methodical: Warden kit sorted by type under a snow tarp, boots in one pile and belts in another. Four sledges stand empty and one is still loaded and roped. There is very little blood anywhere in the snow, and the tidiness of it is worse than the smell would have been.
a1_drag_kit: A Warden signet and a dispatch tube come off the top of the pile, and the tube is still sealed, which is the interesting part of the find. The seal on it is not a Warden seal at all but a Reckoning chapter seal. Nyre identifies whose chapter it is without needing to look at it a second time.
a1_burial: An hour of digging graves in frozen ground with a moor-iron pick, and Nyre says the words properly over nine Wardens while the company stands sweating in a wind that takes the sweat immediately. Dellach faces uphill throughout. It costs the last of the light and buys something that cannot be spent anywhere.
a1_ambush: Two hours lying in snow with the cold coming up through everything, and then nine minutes of violence that goes mostly according to plan. Five Skree lie dead along the trail when it stops. One of them is wearing Warden boots two sizes too large and a bone tally-ring of nine strokes on a thong at the throat.
a1_bog: In a drift-filled adit under the shoulder there is a body standing upright, frozen and perfectly preserved. The hands are bound at the wrist in a knot Ilsabet recognises and does not name. A strip of iron has been laid in the open mouth, deliberately, and the snow above the adit has been undisturbed since autumn.
a1_bog_token: Ilsabet reads the strip by lamplight with her glove off, and pronounces it dwarf-cut, a pay-tally, one of an original nine. The rank cut into the end of it is the ninth hand, the one that keeps the count for the other eight. The die that struck it was cut within the year, she says, because the edges are still sharp.
a1_deadroad: The old drift goes down and west under everything, unlit and unmaintained, its mouth walled to half height by a survey crew that evidently changed its mind and took its own wall down again. Vurma reads the survey marks and translates two of them. The third she reads silently and then says that it is not a survey mark at all.
a1_road_cut: In the open drift the survey pillars stand every hundred feet, and the third one carries nine notches cut beneath the Guild's mark. Beside it a lamp niche holds a clay lamp with oil in it, and the oil has not been standing long enough to gum. Nobody has serviced this drift officially since before Vurma was apprenticed.
a1_niche: The lamp is decanted into your own reservoir, and it is better oil than anything bought at Rell's Gate. Vurma says what everybody has worked out already: somebody services this drift on a schedule, and that somebody will notice a light reservoir long before they notice five people. She says it without lowering her voice, which is her way of arguing.
a1_gallery: The covered gallery is dry and echoes badly, its roof slabs holding everywhere except the far end where a fall has closed the way entirely. While the company stands looking at the fall, something in the rubble of it shifts once, unhurriedly, with the sound of a chair being moved in another room. Then it does not do it again.
a1_gallery_dig: An hour of moving stone by hand with Dellach and Halt at the face and dust in every throat, until the fall gives up a gap wide enough for a shoulder. Air comes out of the gap immediately and steadily. It smells of lamp oil and old meat in roughly equal proportion, and it is warmer than the drift.
a1_crawl: Sixty feet of crawl on your elbows with the roof riding your back, and then the space opens into a chamber. Nine lamp niches, all burnt dry, and nine hooks above them. Beneath the hooks a Reckoning courier sits in a good winter coat with a chapter seal still pinned at the collar and both hands folded in his lap.
a1_seal: Prior Vask's own chapter seal comes away bright, and the dead courier's satchel holds nine requisition slips signed in a hand Nyre has known since childhood. The last of them is dated eleven days ago, which means somebody has been down here since, and has been keeping the paperwork current.
a1_camp: The last camp is the eleventh station, two miles short of the Marchgate, and from its bench you can see nine lamps burning ahead of you in the dark. They have been burning since before the charts say they should. The company's mood has arrived at the specific quiet of people who have stopped asking whether the charts are wrong.
a1_camp_dark: A cold camp with the lamps out, and at the third hour a courier file goes past on the paving below the station. Nine lamps, unhurried, moving in step. At the head of it somebody is counting aloud in a language that appears to have far more numbers in it than any language needs, and the count is the one Kettle set out on a table at Rell's Gate.
a1_camp_fire: One lamp, hot food, dry socks and ninety minutes of sleep each in a dwarf station with a working flue, which is more comfort than this road usually offers anybody. At the end of it there is something standing at the very edge of the lamplight. It does not approach, and it does not leave, and it does not appear to be breathing.
a1_challenge: The challenge is given in the Warden form, three times, as the oath requires now that you are sworn. On the third asking the shape at the edge of the light answers with a number rather than a name. Then it waits, with what could easily be patience, to see whether anybody in the Ninth Sword knows the next one.
a1_scout: Kettle is back at the second hour with a bad colour in her face and a scout's report in order of importance. The Marchgate stands unbarred with its bar set down neatly inside. All nine of its lamps are trimmed, a scraped Warden shield is nailed to the post as a notice, and the snow inside the arch has boot prints going in and none coming out.
a1_slip: The file comes through at the third hour, and the company follows it in at forty paces, moving on the lamp-count off Ossa's charts. Learning the rhythm takes about four minutes and knowing it is worth the whole walk. You arrive at the Marchgate with the leaf still swinging gently from whatever went through it.
a1_follow: Following nine lamps down a dwarf road at forty paces means staying close enough to hear the count, and close enough to hear one member of the file who is plainly not walking under his own management. After a quarter of an hour Ossa says the thing that everybody has worked out and nobody wanted to be first with. The count is not rising; it is going round.
a1_pass_as_nine: The company falls into the file and takes up the count, with Kettle steady on numbers she learned when she was eleven years old. Eleven minutes of walking in that rhythm teaches you the hours, the stations and the intervals better than the charts do. It also teaches you what the file is hauling, and where, and how often.
a1_night_push: Camp is struck at midnight and the last two miles are walked on unlit paving out of nothing but the captain's impatience. The company arrives at the Marchgate grey-faced, short-tempered and with an hour still to wait before anything can usefully be done. Nobody says anything about it, which is its own kind of comment.
a1_approach: The last quarter mile to the Marchgate runs in the open on dwarf paving, with the arch ahead and the Warden's shield on its post catching the lamplight. Nine lamps burn on nine brackets, every one of them trimmed within the hour. In the snow drifted through the arch there are boot prints going in, and there are none at all coming out.
a1_gate: The Marchgate of Sixteen Mile spans the whole road: a dwarf arch with a Warden tower cut into the rock above it, its lintel carved with a door held shut by nine irons. A scraped shield is nailed to the post and nine lamps burn on their brackets, trimmed within the hour. The gate leaf stands unbarred and open a hand's width, with the bar set down neatly on the inside.
a1_watch: A day spent watching a gate teaches the company exactly one thing, and it is worth the day. At the ninth hour two men in Warden cloaks that do not fit them come out through the gap, take down three of the lamps, and carry them back inside again. Neither man puts a hand anywhere near the leaf, and neither of them looks once at the road.
e_a1_gibbet_night: It is a dry warm camp at the fourth station, out of the draught, with a working bracket and a courier's barrow to sit against. At the third hour the file arrives and stops, and a voice begins a count that includes the sleepers by name in the order they lay down. The captain's name comes ninth on the list, which is the last one it needs.
e_a1_beam: The lamp brackets are taken as a dry route across the cistern dip, which works for the first three. The fourth comes out of nine-hundred-year-old mortar with two of the company hanging from it. The water underneath is deeper than the lamps had suggested, and it is going somewhere that the dwarves cut deliberately.
e_a1_swept: The rope is let go in spring water cold enough to stop thought before it stops the hands. The cistern's overflow goes somewhere the dwarves cut on purpose and maintained for nine hundred years. Afterwards the road is exactly as quiet as it was before, and the lamps below the water line go on burning.
e_a1_drown: The pace is kept and the shoulder's second attempt succeeds where the first only made a point. A cornice gives way with three of the company standing on it, the barrow goes with them, and the whiteout closes over the whole business within a minute. Sixteen Mile is two miles off and nobody from the Ninth Sword covers them.
e_a1_fenkin_camp: The small bootprints are followed home to a Skree warren of two hundred under the shoulder, which is about a hundred and ninety more than the plan allowed for. The company is taken alive, because alive is specifically what the warren is paid to deliver. Five more marks go into a tally kept for somebody a long way down the road.
e_a1_fall: The fall is widened properly, because Vurma is right that it should be done once and done correctly with the pick rather than badly with hands. The gallery roof has been holding for a century with considerable patience. It chooses this hour to stop, and forty feet of dwarf work comes down in the time it takes to look up.
e_a1_counted: The next number is given aloud, and the shape at the edge of the lamplight accepts it as an answer and steps into the light to complete the transaction. Whatever the Ninth Sword becomes after that is counted, and kept, and moved down the road on schedule. It is not, in any useful sense, a company any more.
e_a1_kettle_alone: Kettle goes in alone at the second hour, and the gate leaf closes to a thumb's width behind her inside a minute. After four hours of nothing at all the company walks back up the Lamp Road without the only person who could recognise the cadence in the dark. That ends the commission, and something else besides.
e_a1_bram: An hour's sleep, and porters' arithmetic done quietly in the dark. The watch is abandoned somewhere around the second hour, and the barrow goes back up the road with the salt, the spare oil and both reservoirs. The company wakes two miles from the Marchgate with nothing left to walk in with and nothing to walk back on.
e_a1_turn_back: The sensible call is made two miles short of the gate, the report is written honestly, and the fee is returned in full to a Warden who accepts it without comment. It is the correct decision. You will spend nine years hearing Corrow's chartered company tell it differently in every station house on the road.
e_a1_mule: The barrow is sent up the paving ahead of the company as an experiment, on a slight downhill with a rope trailing behind it. It rolls to the arch, stops, stands there for nine seconds, and then goes in through a gap it cannot possibly fit through. The salt and the oil go with it, and the rope comes back cut clean.
